title: U.S. House · South Carolina's 1st District

context.text: This is an open seat: incumbent Nancy Mace (R) withdrew from the Republican primary to run for governor of South Carolina and is not on the general-election ballot. Eighteen candidates (seven Democrats and 11 Republicans) ran in the primaries for the seat.

Nancy Lacore won the Democratic primary runoff on June 23, 2026 with 52.1% of the vote, defeating Mac Deford. Jenny Honeycutt won the Republican primary runoff on June 23, 2026 with 53.7% of the vote, defeating Mark Smith.

candidates.name: Nancy Lacore
candidates.ballotNote: Won the Democratic primary runoff (June 23, 2026) with 52.1% of the vote

priorities.text: Making life more affordable for Lowcountry families by lowering costs of housing, healthcare, prescription drugs, insurance, energy, and childcare, and protecting Social Security and Medicare.
Restoring accountability in Washington: supports banning members of Congress from trading individual stocks and getting dark money out of elections; says she has not taken corporate PAC money.
Improving care for veterans and military families: reducing VA wait times, expanding mental healthcare access, and giving veterans more flexibility to use education benefits.

positions.summary: Supports permanently banning offshore drilling along the South Carolina coast and investing in flood resilience.
positions.quote: I support investing in flood resilience, protecting our waterways and marshes, and permanently banning offshore drilling off our coast.

positions.summary: Her campaign site calls for restoring the enhanced Affordable Care Act premium subsidies and offering all Americans a non-profit, Medicare-like insurance option.
positions.quote: Offer all Americans a non-profit insurance option like Medicare, an insurance that prioritizes patients over profits.

positions.summary: Her campaign site calls for eliminating the current tariffs and supporting targeted trade enforcement instead of blanket tariffs.
positions.quote: Support targeted trade enforcement instead of blanket tariffs.

positions.summary: Her campaign site says she will work to guarantee women's reproductive freedom in law.
positions.quote: I will work to guarantee women’s reproductive freedom in law.

candidates.researchNotes: Positions beyond the offshore-drilling/climate statement (e.g., on abortion, guns, taxes) were not found in the sources reviewed within the research budget.

candidates.name: Jenny Honeycutt
candidates.ballotNote: Won the Republican primary runoff (June 23, 2026) with 53.7% of the vote; endorsed by President Donald Trump

priorities.text: "Standing up for the Lowcountry with principled, America First solutions that strengthen our communities, secure our borders, and protect our way of life."
priorities.quote: Standing up for the Lowcountry with principled, America First solutions that strengthen our communities, secure our borders, and protect our way of life.

priorities.text: Restoring fiscal responsibility by combating wasteful federal spending and working to balance the budget.

positions.summary: Her campaign platform commits her to a ban on transgender athletes in women's sports, using the slogan quoted here.
positions.quote: Jenny is committed to keeping men out of women’s sports.

statements.quote: Jenny believes every life is precious and deserving of protection, and she will be a steadfast advocate for the unborn.
statements.context: On her campaign website platform page, 2026

statements.quote: This includes ensuring our border is secure – stopping the flow of deadly drugs like fentanyl and criminal illegal aliens from harming our families, our neighborhoods, and our economy.
statements.context: On her campaign website platform page, 2026

candidates.researchNotes: Positions and statements from her campaign website platform page; she has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey. Her page mentions the Second Amendment without stating a position on gun laws, so no guns entry was added.

candidates.name: Bill Reeside
candidates.ballotNote: Nominated at the Libertarian Party convention on April 11, 2026

priorities.text: Reducing the federal deficit and reforming Social Security and Medicare onto sound long-term financial footing.
priorities.quote: Republicans and Democrats have rung up $38 trillion in federal debt. The three main culprits: interest payments on the debt itself, impending bankruptcy of Social Security, and Medicare, which is about to be overwhelmed by our aging population.

priorities.text: Overhauling immigration policy, including limits on asylum and temporary protected status while creating a path to citizenship for 'Dreamers.'

Restricting use of the U.S. military: repealing standing Authorizations for Use of Military Force, requiring Congress to declare war under Article One, and barring military use for domestic policing or nation-building.

positions.summary: Says he will legislate to remove all current Authorizations for Use of Military Force and require the executive branch to follow Article One, which gives Congress the power to declare war.
positions.quote: I will legislate to remove all Authorizations for Use of Military Force currently in effect and force the Executive branch to abide by Article One of the Constitution, which gives Congress the power to declare war.

sources.title: Issues & Priorities
sources.publisher: Nancy Lacore for Congress campaign website

researchNotes: Basic-tier research. A write-in independent candidate (Clayton Cuteri) is on Ballotpedia's general-election list but is not included as a full entry; no public record was found for him beyond the ballot listing. Bill Reeside's biography relies on his Ballotpedia survey, a local TV profile and a campaign-supplied news statement; his birthplace and year of birth were not found.
